sources.entry: Traefik - HTTP reverse proxy and load balancer that makes deploying microservices easy. (Source Code) MIT Go/Docker
Traefik | Cloud-native reverse proxy and load balancer with automatic Docker discovery

summary.one_liner: Traefik is a cloud-native HTTP reverse proxy and load balancer that discovers services from orchestrators and registries and configures routes automatically.
summary.what_it_does: Traefik listens to service registries and orchestrator APIs (Docker, Swarm mode, Kubernetes, Consul, Etcd, Rancher v2, Amazon ECS, and a File backend) and generates routes for microservices without manual configuration. It updates its configuration continuously without restarts. It supports multiple load balancing algorithms, circuit breakers and retries, and can obtain HTTPS certificates via Let's Encrypt, including wildcard certificates. It handles WebSocket, HTTP/2 and gRPC traffic, exposes metrics (Prometheus, Datadog, Statsd, InfluxDB 2.X), writes access logs in JSON or CLF, and provides a REST API and a web UI. Routes can also be configured manually if preferred.
use_cases: route traffic to microservices in Docker or Kubernetes
load balance HTTP and gRPC services
expose containers behind a single entry point
collect proxy metrics and access logs
how_to_run: Download the latest binary from the releases page and run: ./traefik --configFile=traefik.toml
Or run the Docker image: docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -p 80:80 -v $PWD/traefik.toml:/etc/traefik/traefik.toml traefik
Or get the sources: git clone (repository URL), then build from source
Follow the 5-Minute Quickstart in the documentation (requires Docker)
notable: Automatic, dynamic configuration from orchestrators and service registries without restarts
Single binary distributed as a tiny official Docker image
Built-in Let's Encrypt support with wildcard certificates
Web UI and REST API for inspecting routes
caveats: Migrating between major versions may involve breaking changes; the README points to a migration guide
Commercial support is offered by Traefik.io separately from the community forum
README documents only the Docker quickstart and binary run; detailed setup is in external documentation
